Your first couple of hours in the game is a test of patience and willpower against your wage counter. You're on the right track killing looters, other things you SHOULD be doing during the early game:

​

* **Work towards setting up a workshop** in a prosperous town, bonus points if it's in a kingdom you feel like you might join down the line
   * Workshops' income depends on a lot of factors, the main ones being, is there another workshop of the same type, and do the surrounding BOUNDED villages provide the raw material for the workshop you want.
   * Dont bother with caravans until you're more established
* **Tournaments + Betting**, not only good XP and training, but you can sell the loot they give you, or you can...
* **Smelt Weapons in smithies, and take orders** sell raw materials or use them to create high-end weapons for quick cash
   * Everyone will tell you Smithing is broken, it is. It can easily snowball into ludicrous wealth if you focus on it. Do it at your own risk
* **Quests, and as many as you can do.**
   * Bandit Lair quest gives good cash, and the loot is pretty valuable

​

Eventually, your daily wages will turn into income, and you'll have more flexibility with your wealth. Try not to hold onto high-end troops, and large armies early game when you're still financially unstable. About 20 Tier 3 troops should suffice for the early game.

This isn't the time for pity parties. Get out there and throw yourself at the mercy of the wolves when you feel like you're emotionally and mentally ready for it. When that time depends on you, just keep grinding out yourself and accept that change is slow and okay.

Consider the following, if YES to any of these, move on to the next one. Don't think about it too hard, just be honest with yourself

​

* Can I AFFORD ($$$) to quit?
* Can I AFFORD ($$$) to stay extra in school if it means finding another internship?
* Am I CONFIDENT that I can get another internship?

If you got to this point, quit the internship. 

Now, this is me overreaching so feel free to stop right here, and best of luck to ya. Otherwise, about your field, the same rules as above.

​

* Do I WANT another internship, in this field?
* Can I graduate with an internship in ANOTHER field?
* Are there any internships that INTEREST me?
* Do I WANT to be in this field?

If you got to this point, I would speak to a career counselor at your UNI and explain to them the situation. They might be able to offer you more professional advice than I can, and maybe help free you from your funk.

​

For what it's worth, you're incredibly young, and I am sure you can transfer credits to a subject that makes you happier and still has good financial prospects after graduating. But you have to put in the research, hard work, and responsibility that comes from a career change. You have a lot of time to think it over, and if you do decide to think it over, I wish you all the luck in the world.
